Installation is limited to copying extension files into the appropriate GNOME Shell extensions directory.

The package follows standard AUR packaging practices: it uses a pinned Git commit, verifies integrity with a strong checksum, and performs a straightforward build and install. While the extension's functionality (clipboard history) may involve access to user data, that is within the scope of its intended purpose and not indicative of malicious supply-chain behavior in the packaging.
